title: Western Hemisphere surge anticipation scratchpad - July 18 2029
content:
Purpose: informal working notes for Western Hemisphere surge anticipation. Use this as a single source-of-truth for the next 7-day prewarming/backfill plan, quick experiments, and open questions for the infra sync. This is intentionally rough.

Context:
- Recent traffic spikes from a major customer in NA and a marketing campaign in SA create a likely 2-4x short-term uplift for chat endpoints starting ~2029-07-21 00:00 UTC.
- We need a low-friction hedging plan that preserves latency SLOs for paid customers and keeps unit cost growth bounded.
- This doc ties into the global surge playbook but focuses on Western Hemisphere specifics (latency corridors, cloud regions, and cross-region backfill).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Recommended prewarm schedule: +60 GPUs in us-central1 and +30 GPUs in us-west1 on 2029-07-20 03:00 UTC (24h prewarm window), and +20 GPUs in sa-east1 on 2029-07-20 05:00 UTC.
- Reserve 15% of burst capacity as non-preemptible reserved pool for latency-critical tenants (apply reserved tag: latency-critical-west).
- Enable predictive preemption buffer in EdgePredict v2 with horizon=30m for chat-heavy routes.
- Run canary traffic through dedicated hedged region (us-west1) at 10% to validate inference fallbacks and KV cache priming.

Raw notes from standup (2029-07-18 09:30 PT):
- Marcus: observed pattern of short TTL queries from customer X that warm KV cache fast, but cause uneven batching; edge LBs in us-west1 show queue depth spikes around 00:00-02:00 UTC.
- Priya: tooling to snapshot KV cache state for priming exists but needs packaging into a cron job; current approach is manual.
- Diego: preemptible pool in sa-east1 has free capacity but start time >= 12m; recommend a small non-preemptible pool for first 30 minutes after surge.
- Ava: flagged that the cost model underestimates long-tail API calls; will add a conservative multiplier for cost projection.

Numbers to know (quick):
- Baseline steady-state GPU usage (Western Hemisphere): 420 GPUs (avg).
- Predicted surge peak window: 2029-07-21 00:00 to 2029-07-21 04:00 UTC.
- Surge uplift estimate: +110 GPUs (50th pct), +220 GPUs (90th pct).
- Proposed prewarm target (to hit SLO): +110 GPUs distributed: us-central1:+60, us-west1:+30, sa-east1:+20.
- Suggested reserved non-preemptible pool: 15 GPUs for high-priority customers in NA, 5 GPUs in SA.

Operational play snippets:
- Prewarm play: create 'surge-west-2029-07-21' fleet with autoscaling min=110 for window 2029-07-20 03:00 UTC to 2029-07-22 03:00 UTC. Set graceful-drain=180s, eviction-policy=prefer-preemptible.
- Prime cache: run one shot prefix-prime job per model version used by chat routes; target top 10 prompt prefixes from last 48h.
- Canary: route 10% traffic to hedged variant in us-west1 for first hour after start. Monitor p50/p95 token latency and KV misses.

Experiment log: EdgePredict v2 backtest (short):
- Model trained on 6 weeks of queue-depth features + external calendar signals.
- Backtest on 2029-06-01..2029-07-15 shows recall of surge windows 0.82, lead time median 22m.
- False positives: ~1.6 per week per region; these were low-cost (used preemptible) but raised ephemeral tickets due to noisy autoscaling.
- Next step: tune threshold to favor fewer false positives; add a manual veto API for on-call.

Open questions / risks:
1) Cost vs SLO tradeoff: if we prewarm full 90th pct lift, cost increases by ~18% for the 48h window. Is that acceptable for sales/finance? (Action: Ava to sync with FinOps by 2029-07-18 EOD)
2) Cross-region KV priming consistency: priming in us-central may not help us-west KV cache; need prefix replication or warm-forwarding. Short term: run priming jobs in each region. (Owner: Marcus)
3) Preemptible start latency in SA: measured >=12m in last run — too slow for short surges. Options: buy small non-preemptible pool, or throttle ingress to SA during first 10m. (Owner: Diego)
4) Canary rollback SLAs: if canary p95 > baseline p95 + 30%, automated rollback should trigger. Verify rollback path end-to-end. (Owner: Priya)

Action items (with owners):
- Ava: draft quick cost memo for FinOps and Sales showing delta for prewarm options (conservative, balanced, full). Due 2029-07-18 17:00.
- Marcus: create automated priming cron in us-central1/us-west1/sa-east1 and test on model v2029-07-10. Link PR and schedule. Due 2029-07-19 10:00. Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/218
- Diego: reserve 20 GPUs non-preemptible in sa-east1 for 48h window and test eviction behavior. Due 2029-07-20 00:00. Jira: INFRA-4231
- Priya: wire up canary monitor dashboards and add p95+p50+KV-miss panel; add automated rollback runbook. Due 2029-07-20 08:00.
- On-call: prepare 2hr shift coverage around 2029-07-21 00:00 UTC; rotate primary = @infra-oncall-west.

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider a small sticky-routing rule for VIP customers to prefer hedged pool for first 10m after surge start. Could reduce cross-region cold starts.
- If EdgePredict v2 gives 20-30m lead time, we can reduce expensive full prewarm to a staged prewarm: stage1=30% prewarm, stage2=100% one hour before.
- Need to update cost model to include long-tail token multiplier 1.12x for chat endpoints pinned to large contexts.

Meeting checkpoints (next 48h):
- 2029-07-18 16:00 PT: Sync w/ FinOps (Ava + Sales rep) to confirm acceptable spend cap.
- 2029-07-19 09:00 PT: Dry-run priming job validation and canary pipeline smoke test (Marcus + Priya).
- 2029-07-20 02:30 PT: Final prewarm go/no-go (all).

Historic references / useful links:
- Prior surge that failed to prewarm properly: incident-2028-11-09 postmortem (Confluence). Observations: delayed priming, overreliance on preemptible-only strategies.
- Backfill playbook v1: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Backfill+Playbook+v1

Misc friction items we should fix post-mortem if this lands:
- Make priming cron configurable per-region via Console UI.
- Centralize prewarm ops so that Sales can request reserved pools via a short form (reduce manual infra tickets).
- Improve observability of KV cache heat: currently only p95 misses and hit-rate by model; need per-prefix heat map.

If you see something missing, add a note below and tag @Ava. This will be the working pad until 2029-07-22 when we convert to a formal runbook.

-- Ava
